strings.title: Add Up to Subtract
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When two numbers are close together, find the difference by counting up from the smaller one through friendly numbers.
strings.keywords: difference, distance, count up, next ten, friendly number
watchFor: Bigger minus smaller in each place (92 − 68 = 36): ask "Is 68 + 36 equal to 92?"
Counting up but forgetting a jump: ask "Which jumps make the answer?"
Taking away 486 from 503: ask "Are these close together? How far apart?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "When is counting up quicker than taking away?" Land: when the numbers are close, the difference is the distance. Jump to the next ten or hundred, then on, and add the jumps.

problems.notes: Look for: 75 up 5 to 80, up 10 to 90. Ask: "Hold on to this: how far from 75 to 90?" Model: numberline 75 >80 >90
Look for: the same jumps, then 2 more. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Model: numberline 75 >80 >92
Look for: 68 up 2 to 70, up 22 to 92. Ask: "What's the next ten after 68?" Word choice: "the distance between". Model: numberline 68 >70 >92

responses.tip: Bigger minus smaller in each place. Ask: is 68 + 36 = 92?

problems.notes: Look for: 3 to 90, 10 to 100, 50 to 150. Ask: "Which friendly numbers did you land on?" Model: numberline 87 >90 >100 >150

responses.tip: Ask: add the jumps again. Is 87 + 73 = 150?

problems.notes: Look for: 4 to 490, 10 to 500, 3 more. Ask: "Are these close together?" Model: numberline 486 >490 >500 >503

responses.tip: Regrouping slip. Ask: are 503 and 486 close together?

problems.notes: Context: "How many years from 1985 to 2010?" Look for: 15 to 2000, 10 more. Ask: "What's the first friendly number?" Model: numberline 1985 >1990 >2000 >2010
Look for: 25 to 10 000, then 2 more. Ask: "Does it work with big numbers too?" Model: numberline 9975 >10000 >10002

strings.title: Take Too Much, Then Add Back
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: When the number you take away is just under a friendly number, take the friendly number, then add back the extra. It works the same way with decimals: 6.4 − 1.9 is 6.4 − 2 + 0.1.
strings.keywords: take away a friendly number, add back, compensate, too much, decimals
watchFor: Taking the extra away as well (84 − 19 = 84 − 20 − 1): ask "Did you take away too much or too little?"
Adding back the wrong amount with decimals (7.25 − 2.99 = 7.25 − 3 + 0.1): ask "How far is 2.99 from 3?"
Using the algorithm with lots of regrouping: ask "Is 2.99 close to a whole number?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why do we add back?" Land: we took away more than we needed to, so the extra goes back. Same move for whole numbers and decimals: 6.4 − 1.9 = 6.4 − 2 + 0.1.

problems.notes: Look for: 2 tens away. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: numberline 84 -20
Look for: take 20, give 1 back. Ask: "How does the last one help?" Word choice: "took too much". Model: numberline 84 -20 +1

responses.tip: Took the extra away too. Ask: too much or too little?

problems.notes: Look for: take 40, give 1 back. Ask: "What's the same?" Model: numberline 84 -40 +1
Look for: just the ones change. Ask: "Hold on to this one too." Model: numberline 6.4 -2
Look for: take 2, give 0.1 back. Ask: "Is it the same move with decimals?" Model: numberline 6.4 -2 +0.1

responses.tip: Ask: did taking 2 take too much or too little?

problems.notes: Look for: take 3, give 0.01 back. Ask: "How far is 2.99 from 3?" Model: numberline 7.25 -3 +0.01

responses.tip: Added back a tenth. Ask: is 2.99 a tenth or a hundredth away from 3?

problems.notes: Look for: take 5, give 0.2 back. Ask: "What's 4.8 close to?" Model: numberline 15.3 -5 +0.2

strings.title: Big Numbers, Same Difference
strings.label: Bank
strings.strategy: Add the same amount to both numbers so you subtract a friendly one. It works the same way with numbers up to 100 000: 73 002 − 47 996 is 73 006 − 48 000.
strings.keywords: same difference, slide, friendly number, thousands, ten thousands
watchFor: Moving the numbers in opposite directions (5002 − 2998 to 5000 − 3000): ask "Did the distance between them stay the same?"
Regrouping across lots of zeros: ask "Is 9998 close to a friendly number?"
Losing place value in big numbers: ask "Which digit is the ten thousands?"
strings.wrapUp: Ask "Why does adding the same to both keep the answer?" Land: the difference is the distance between them, and sliding both the same way keeps the distance. Slide until you subtract a friendly number.

problems.notes: Look for: 5 thousands take 3 thousands. Ask: "Hold on to this." Model: numberline 3000 >5000
Look for: add 2 to both: 5004 − 3000. Ask: "What does 2998 need?" Word choice: "same difference". Model: slide 5002 - 2998 = 5004 - 3000

responses.tip: Moved them in opposite directions. Ask: did the distance change?

problems.notes: Look for: add 3 to both: 10 003 − 7000. Ask: "Why is this easier than the algorithm?" Model: slide 10000 - 6997 = 10003 - 7000
Look for: add 2 to both: 24 007 − 10 000. Ask: "What's 9998 close to?" Model: slide 24005 - 9998 = 24007 - 10000
Look for: add 5 to both. Ask: "How much do you add?" Model: slide 50000 - 29995 = 50005 - 30000
Look for: add 4 to both: 73 006 − 48 000. Ask: "Does it still work?" Model: slide 73002 - 47996 = 73006 - 48000
Look for: add 1 to both: 100 001 − 65 000. Ask: "Which number should be friendly?" Model: slide 100000 - 64999 = 100001 - 65000
